events.title: Spring Boot 1.0 released
events.summary: Pivotal released Spring Boot 1.0 on April 1, 2014 — opinionated auto-configuration for Spring apps with embedded servers and starter dependencies.
events.about: Spring Boot (`java -jar app.jar`) eliminated XML boilerplate: starters bundle dependencies, auto-config wires beans, and Actuator exposes health checks. Microservices teams ship REST APIs and batch jobs without application servers; it became the default way new Java backends start in the 2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: Spring Boot made Spring as fast to start as Ruby or Node microframeworks.
narrative.whyImportant: Embedded Tomcat/Jetty and starter POMs defined the containerless Java deployment model.
narrative.problemSolved: Spring apps required heavy WAR deployments and pages of XML before writing business logic.

sources.title: Spring Blog — Spring Boot 1.0 GA Released (April 1, 2014)

events.title: TypeScript 1.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft released TypeScript 1.0 on April 2, 2014 — the first stable version of Anders Hejlsberg's typed JavaScript superset.
events.about: TypeScript 1.0 gave teams optional types, classes, and modules that compiled to ES5 JavaScript for any browser. It laid the groundwork for Angular 2+, VS Code, and the gradual typing approach that now dominates large front-end codebases.

narrative.whyChosen: TypeScript 1.0 proved typed JavaScript could ship in production without a new runtime.
narrative.whyImportant: It established the compile-to-JS pattern that frameworks and IDEs built on.
narrative.problemSolved: Large JavaScript projects lacked static checking and scalable module structure.

events.title: Brendan Eich resigns as Mozilla CEO
events.summary: Brendan Eich resigned as Mozilla CEO on April 3, 2014 after only days in the role — controversy over a political donation.
events.about: Eich created JavaScript in ten days in 1995 and later co-founded Brave. His brief Mozilla tenure and exit showed how founder-legends intersect with modern corporate governance and community politics.

narrative.whyChosen: Eich embodies JavaScript's creation and a dramatic open-source leadership moment.
narrative.whyImportant: It raised questions about separating creators' personal views from their technical legacy.
narrative.problemSolved: Mozilla faced community trust crisis immediately after appointing a co-founder as CEO.

events.title: Express 4.0 released
events.summary: Express 4.0 shipped on April 9, 2014 — removing Connect middleware bundling and stabilizing the router for production Node APIs.
events.about: Express 4 split built-in middleware into separate packages and fixed the router — the version that powered the MEAN stack and early REST microservices. Most Node tutorials and boilerplates still trace back to Express 4's API surface.

narrative.whyChosen: Express 4 was the stable baseline for Node web APIs through the 2010s.
narrative.whyImportant: A cleaner router and middleware model defined how Node handles HTTP.
narrative.problemSolved: Express 3 bundled deprecated Connect middleware and had router edge cases in production.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy S5 released
events.summary: Samsung began selling the Samsung Galaxy S5 — water resistance and a fingerprint sensor in a plastic flagship body.
events.about: The Galaxy S series remained Android's volume flagship counterweight to iPhone. Water resistance and a fingerprint sensor in a plastic flagship body. Developers testing Android builds routinely validated on Galaxy S hardware as the default non-Pixel reference.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy S5 continued Samsung's annual Android flagship cadence.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy S devices set the hardware bar millions of Android users and developers encounter.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed consistent premium hardware for testing flagship features each year.

events.title: Tom Preston-Werner resigns from GitHub
events.summary: GitHub co-founder Tom Preston-Werner resigned on April 21, 2014 after an internal investigation into workplace conduct.
events.about: Preston-Werner co-created GitHub, Jekyll, and Semantic Versioning — but his departure forced GitHub to add formal management after years of a flat structure. The episode marked a turning point in Silicon Valley workplace culture discourse.

narrative.whyChosen: Preston-Werner's exit ended GitHub's founder-led flat organization era.
narrative.whyImportant: It prompted GitHub to institutionalize management and HR processes at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: A bossless culture lacked accountability mechanisms when internal conflicts escalated.

events.title: OnePlus One released
events.summary: OnePlus released the OnePlus One — flagship specs at mid-range price — CyanogenMod-era disruptor.
events.about: The phone expanded Android's flagship landscape beyond Samsung and Google. Flagship specs at mid-range price — cyanogenmod-era disruptor.

narrative.whyChosen: The OnePlus One was a significant Android flagship.
narrative.whyImportant: Diverse Android flagships gave developers multiple hardware targets beyond Galaxy and Pixel.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed credible flagship alternatives to Samsung and carrier-skinned phones.

events.title: Gavin Wood coins the term Web3
events.summary: Ethereum co-founder Gavin Wood coined "Web 3.0" in April 2014 — describing decentralized apps that run without trusting a central server.
events.about: Wood's vision paired blockchains, peer-to-peer messaging, and decentralized storage so users owned identity and data instead of platforms. The label became marketing shorthand for wallets, NFTs, and token-gated apps — loved by founders, mocked by skeptics, but the name stuck.

narrative.whyChosen: Web3 named the post-platform internet Ethereum builders were pitching.
narrative.whyImportant: It framed crypto as infrastructure for apps, not just digital gold.
narrative.problemSolved: Web 2.0 centralized user data in a handful of companies; builders wanted an alternative architecture.
